title: RenderAPI: per-draw tex_env (REPLACE/ADD) for HUD icons and additive glow
description:
Context: draw_state_from() pins tex_env = GL_MODULATE (src/backend/desktop/render_gl.c:77); GL_REPLACE/GL_ADD are unreachable. The gfx state manager already diffs tex_env (src/backend/desktop/gfx_gl.c:147) - only the frame cannot express it.

Change:
- RDraw gains `int tex_env;` (0 = MODULATE, 1 = REPLACE, 2 = ADD; default MODULATE), plumbed through draw_state_from() into GfxState.tex_env.
- REPLACE: HUD icons / decal text where vertex colour must not darken the texture. ADD: additive glow (beacon, spray highlights).
- Keep the whitelist to MODULATE/REPLACE/ADD only - everything else (DECAL, BLEND, COMBINE) is not portable: the GE supports only its TENV modes, and the PVR has no TENV (the DC backend maps ADD to a blend mode instead, e.g. src PVR_BLEND_ONE / dst PVR_BLEND_ONE).

Done when: an additive sprite renders glow-correct on desktop; the whitelist survives the backend split.

comments.author: mcp-agent
comments.text:
## Audit context (2026-10-03, docs/render.md)

draw_state_from() pins tex_env = GL_MODULATE (src/backend/desktop/render_gl.c:77); gfx_set() already diffs tex_env (src/backend/desktop/gfx_gl.c:147) — only the frame cannot express other modes. Use cases: REPLACE for HUD icons/decal text (vertex colour must not darken the texture), ADD for additive glow (beacon, spray highlights).

## Hardware mapping (verified against SDK sources)

- Desktop: glTexEnvi(GL_TEXTURE_ENV, GL_TEXTURE_ENV_MODE, mode) — plumbing exists in gfx_set.
- PSP: texture function sceGuTexFunc(GU_TFX_*, GU_TCC_*); additive glow can also be a blend op (GU_ADD with GU_FIX factors; the pspsdk blend sample enumerates ADD/SUBTRACT/REVERSE_SUBTRACT/MIN/MAX/ABS with GU_SRC_ALPHA/GU_ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA/GU_FIX).
- Dreamcast: PVR_TXRENV_REPLACE confirmed (px = ARGB(tex)) alongside MODULATE (px = A(tex) + RGB(col)*RGB(tex)), DECAL and MODULATEALPHA (KOS dc/pvr/pvr_header.h). GL_ADD has no TXRENV equivalent — map ADD to blending: src PVR_BLEND_ONE + dst PVR_BLEND_ONE with blend enabled (per-header src_enable/dst_enable), like the KOS bumpmap example's DESTCOLOR tricks.

## Whitelist rationale

MODULATE / REPLACE / ADD only. DECAL, BLEND, COMBINE are not portable: the GE has only its TFX modes and the PVR only the four TXRENV modes. Anything else must be expressed as flag combinations or pre-baked colours.

Done when: an additive sprite renders glow-correct on desktop; the whitelist survives the backend split (TFX/TXRENV mapping verified on emulators).

title: Wake trail starts under the car and runs too long

comments.author: mcp-agent
comments.text:
## Cause

`trail_push(s_veh.pos)` (src/core/game.c) recorded the car's **origin**, and `emit_wake` builds the ribbon straight over those points. The hull spans local z in [-2, +2] with +Z forward, so the ribbon's head sat under the middle of the car and covered its front half — it read as centred, or as starting ahead of the car.

Length was pure `TRAIL_MAX * TRAIL_STEP`: 64 * 1.1 = 69 units, 2.5 s of wake at the 28 m/s top speed (car.h CAR_MAX_FWD).

## Fix

- Push a point one `WAKE_OFFSET` (2.2, just past the 2.0 hull half-length) behind the car along its heading, so the wake starts at the stern.
- `TRAIL_MAX` 64 -> 20, i.e. 22 units / ~0.8 s at top speed.

Only `s_trail[0]`/`s_trail[1]` (x/z) are read by `trail_push`, so the y component of the pushed point is ignored and `emit_wake` still rebuilds height from `wave_height`.

Build clean, `meson test -C build` 8/8.

comments.author: mcp-agent
comments.text: Note: TRAIL_MAX was 64 when this session started but was already edited to 32 in the working tree by the time the fix landed, so the diff on disk reads 32 -> 20. The 64 figure above is what the original value was.

title: Input layer audit: restore digital fallback, neutralise stale input on controller loss
description:
## Audit (2026-10-03, input contract island1-ibqg / psp island1-rggc / dc island1-19s3)

Verified green first: 7/7 desktop tests, layering guard clean, and desktop/psp/dc all compile and link (psp -> EBOOT.PBP, dc -> island.cdi).

### Hardware facts re-verified against the installed SDKs
- **PSP**: `PSP_CTRL_RTRIGGER = 0x000200` **does exist** (pspsdk `pspctrl.h:60`). The note on island1-rggc claiming "there is no PSP_CTRL_R constant" is wrong and should be retracted. Lx/Ly are 0..255, centre 128 - the `NUB_CENTER/NUB_RANGE` mapping is right. Analog axes require `PSP_CTRL_MODE_ANALOG`, which `backend_input_init` sets.
- **Dreamcast**: `cont_state_t.ltrig/rtrig` are 0..255 with no offset, and KOS **subtracts 128 from joyx/joyy** when it cooks the raw frame (`kernel/arch/dreamcast/hardware/maple/controller.c:176-179`), so a centred stick really does read 0 - `stick_axis()` is correct and there is no phantom full-lock. `buttons` is already inverted by KOS, so masks are active-high as used. Standard pad triggers are 0/255 (digital); a VMU gives true analog, and `/255.0f` handles both.
- Both builds are clean after the mode-aware mapping change: `input_dc.c`/`input_psp.c` including `game.h` is fine (backend -> core is the allowed direction).

### Bugs found in the uncommitted mode-aware remap

1. **The digital `ACT_THROTTLE`/`ACT_BRAKE` fallback is gone on both consoles.** The core contract (island1-553a) keeps those actions as the digital twin of the axes, and `game.c` still reads them: the dev free-fly cam is driven by `input_held(ACT_THROTTLE)`-`input_held(ACT_BRAKE)` (game.c:666) and its slow-speed mode by `input_held(ACT_BRAKE)` (game.c:658). Neither console backend emits them any more, so on PSP/Dreamcast **the dev fly cam cannot move or slow down**. Emitting the digital action alongside the axis in DRIVE mode restores it (core already does `fmaxf(axis, held)`).

2. **PSP R is double-bound**: `ACT_DEV_CAM` (input_psp.c:73) *and* the drive-mode brake axis (input_psp.c:92). Braking toggles the camera. `ACT_DEV_RESET` still has no binding as a result.

3. **Stale input when the controller is not readable.** `backend_input_poll()` returns early if the DC has no maple device (input_dc.c:71,72) or the PSP peek fails (input_psp.c:62). Axes are absolute and latched from `s_pending_axis`, so a pad unplugged mid-drive leaves the throttle pinned at its last value and the car drives away on its own. Both backends must neutralise (release actions, zero axes) instead of returning.

4. **`stick_axis(signed char, ...)` vs KOS's `int` fields** (input_dc.c:51 vs `dc/maple/controller.h:172`). Harmless for -128..127 today, but it truncates silently if a device reports wider.

## Change
- input_psp.c / input_dc.c: emit digital throttle/brake in DRIVE mode next to the axes; neutralise on a failed/absent poll; move the PSP dev bindings off the brake trigger onto VOLUP (dev cam) / VOLDOWN (dev reset); take `int` in the DC axis helper.
- Tests stay GL-free; `meson test -C build` must stay 7/7 and all three platforms must still build.

### Design note (not fixed here)
The mode-aware mapping puts gameplay-mode knowledge in each console backend. That duplicates a decision the core could own (the core already knows the mode, and desktop needs no such branch because W/S means both). Acceptable for now, but if a third platform lands this is the thing to fold into core.

comments.author: mcp-agent
comments.text:
Done. All three platforms build clean (no warnings) and 7/7 desktop tests pass, layering guard included.

**input_psp.c / input_dc.c**
- Triggers/levers now raise the digital `ACT_THROTTLE`/`ACT_BRAKE` alongside the axes, via `update_triggers()` / `update_levers()`. Those track the *emitted* action state rather than the raw hardware, so on foot the actions are released while the edge trackers stay in sync — grabbing the car with a lever already pulled still fires a fresh press. Restores the dev free-fly cam (game.c:666) and its slow-speed mode (game.c:658) on both consoles.
- `neutral_input()` replaces the early `return` on a failed poll (absent maple device, PSP peek failure): it releases every action the table can raise and zeroes steer/throttle/brake, so an unplugged pad can no longer leave the throttle pinned and the car driving off. Both `backend_input_init`s reset the new trackers.
- PSP: dev bindings moved off the brake trigger (R was `ACT_DEV_CAM` *and* the drive-mode brake) onto Vol+ / Vol-, which finally gives `ACT_DEV_RESET` the binding it was missing.
- DC: dev fly cam on **B**, the only free face button. Deliberately *not* on Z/D/C — those are VMU-only and KOS inverts the raw button word (`cooked->buttons = (~raw->buttons) & 0xffff`), so a bit a standard pad never drives can read back as permanently held.
- DC: `stick_axis()` takes `int`, matching `cont_state_t` (was `signed char`, which would truncate silently).

`render_dc.c` changes in the working tree (PVR bin sizes, HUD onto the punch-through list, `pvr_prim`/`pvr_list_*` error logging) are render-side and were left as-is.

Still open: the mode-aware mapping lives in each console backend rather than in core — see the design note in the description.

close_reason: Fixed and verified: digital throttle/brake fallback restored on both consoles, neutral_input() on controller loss, PSP R double-binding removed, DC stick_axis takes int. All 3 platforms build warning-free, 7/7 tests pass.

title: Prop LOD / distance cull so far props simplify or fade into fog
description:
User request: add a LOD system for props so further-away props become simpler or fade into fog.

Context: props (houses, depot, residents, parcel) are emitted at full detail every frame regardless of distance (emit_houses/emit_depot/emit_residents/emit_parcel in src/core/game.c). Distance fog runs FOG_START 40 -> FOG_END 220 (render.h), so anything past ~220 is invisible anyway - drawing it wastes verts/draws against the R_MAX_VERTS/DRAWS caps (island1-41ct). Camera position is available in core (s_chase.pos / s_cam.pos).

Plan:
- Add a core LOD helper (e.g. src/core/lod.h, header-only) that maps squared distance to an LOD level: NEAR = full mesh, MID = simplified mesh (box only, no roof/trim/resident details), FAR = culled (fades into fog).
- Give each prop a distance budget; cull past a max draw distance <= FOG_END so nothing pops (the fog already hides the cut).
- Houses: emit full house (body+gable+door+eaves) when near; emit just the body box at mid; skip at far. Residents: skip when beyond LOD distance (tiny, unseen). Depot sign/trim likewise.
- Keep it core-only and GL-free; verify via api_smoke draw/vert counts at a far camera vs near camera (far should drop R_PASS_PROPS draws).

Done when: standing far from an island, props are simplified/culled while the near view is unchanged, with counts asserted in a test.

comments.author: mcp-agent
comments.text: Done. New header src/core/lod.h: LodLevel {NEAR,MID,FAR} + lod_level(dx,dz) using squared XZ distance from the active camera; LOD_NEAR_DIST=80 (full), LOD_CULL_DIST=200 (inside FOG_END 220, so the cut is ~89% fogged and hidden). game_render samples s_cam_pos from the chase or fly camera each frame. Houses: NEAR=s_house (full), MID=s_house_lod (new body-only box built alongside the full mesh), FAR=skip. Residents draw only within NEAR (tiny, so culled early). Depot and parcel cull at FAR (parcel uses world[3] translation so it also works while strapped to the car). Beacon/car/HUD are untouched (objective markers must stay visible). api-smoke moved the vehicle to (-200,-200) and asserts props near=7 / far=0 while the car still draws (veh=144 verts). All 7 tests pass; runtime smoke clean.

title: Dreamcast input backend (VMU)
description:
Dreamcast VMU/controller backend implementing the input contract (island1-ibqg): backend_input_init/poll fills InputState.

Hardware: D-pad (plus-shaped) . concave analog stick with octagonal gate . green A / blue B / yellow X / red Y face buttons . single round Start . L/R triggers (analog on a VMU, digital 0/255 on a standard pad).

**Provisional mapping in the issue body is SUPERSEDED** — see the 2026-10-05 comment for what the code actually does (levers are the throttle/brake, mode-aware).

Original provisional mapping (per island1-ibqg, now obsolete):
  A -> ACT_THROTTLE . B -> ACT_BRAKE . L -> ACT_BOOST (analog fine)
  Y -> ACT_INTERACT . X -> ACT_VEHICLE
  stick X -> AX_STEER . D-pad: steer override when stick in deadzone
  Start -> ACT_PAUSE
vmu polling for the analog stick + triggers.

Done when: log harness (emulator / dev board) shows correct held/pressed/axis for every button.

comments.author: mcp-agent
comments.text:
## Mapping superseded + input audit (2026-10-05)

### What the code does now (mode-aware, per `game_mode()`)
  L lever -> AX_THROTTLE + digital ACT_THROTTLE   (vehicle only, `ltrig`/255)
  R lever -> AX_BRAKE + digital ACT_BRAKE         (vehicle only, `rtrig`/255)
  A -> ACT_BOOST   Y -> ACT_INTERACT   X -> ACT_VEHICLE   B -> ACT_DEV_CAM
  Start -> ACT_PAUSE . A+B+X+Y+Start -> ACT_QUIT
  stick X -> AX_STEER (deadzone 0.30, remapped) . stick Y -> fwd/back on foot only
  D-pad -> steer override when the stick is centred

Vehicle = levers only. On foot = stick only, with the levers' digital actions released and their edge trackers kept in sync so re-entering the car with a lever already pulled still registers.

### Hardware facts verified against this KOS install
- **KOS already centres the stick**: `cooked->joyx = ((int)raw->joyx) - 128` (`kernel/arch/dreamcast/hardware/maple/controller.c:176-179`), so `stick_axis()` reading 0 at rest is correct — there is no phantom full-lock to guard against. Range is -128..127 and `cont_state_t` declares the fields as `int` (`dc/maple/controller.h:172-176`), so the helper takes `int` now, not `signed char`.
- `ltrig`/`rtrig` are 0..255 with **no** offset. A standard pad reports 0 or 255 (so `/255` gives a clean 0/1), a VMU gives true analog. `TRIGGER_THRESHOLD 128` covers both for the digital twin.
- **Buttons are inverted by KOS** (`cooked->buttons = (~raw->buttons) & 0xffff`), so the `CONT_*` masks are used active-high as written. This is also why nothing is bound to Z/D/C: they only exist on a VMU, and a bit a standard pad never drives can read back as permanently held. B is the only genuinely free button and it takes the dev fly cam.

`maple_enum_type(0, MAPLE_FUNC_CONTROLLER)` + `maple_dev_status()` on port 0; a missing pad now calls `neutral_input()` instead of returning, so an unplugged controller cannot leave the throttle pinned (island1-149l). Cross-builds clean, no warnings.

### Still missing vs done-when
No log harness yet. Note the bindings and deadzones (0.30) have changed since the provisional table, and the analog-vs-digital lever difference between a standard pad and a VMU is worth exercising on both.

comments.author: mcp-agent
comments.text:
## Correction: R accelerates, L brakes (user direction, 2026-10-05)

Supersedes the lever direction in the comment above. The user asked for the usual console convention (Xbox/PlayStation put the accelerator on the **right** trigger), so the levers are swapped:

  R lever (rtrig) -> AX_THROTTLE (`rtrig`/255) + digital ACT_THROTTLE   (vehicle only)
  L lever (ltrig) -> AX_BRAKE (`ltrig`/255) + digital ACT_BRAKE         (vehicle only)

Both the analog axis (input_dc.c:175-176) and the digital twin (`update_levers()`, input_dc.c:95-96) were swapped together, so the axis and the action fallback can never disagree. `update_levers()`'s parameters and the edge trackers were renamed to role-based names (`throttle_raw`/`brake_raw`, `s_prev_throttle`/`s_prev_brake`) rather than side-based (`ltrig`/`rtrig`) — keying by role is what stops the two getting transposed later.

Worth noting the swap is nearly free here: a standard pad's L and R report 0/255 (digital), so the lever values are unaffected; only a VMU's true analog levers change sides.

Everything else is unchanged (A = boost, Y = interact, X = vehicle, B = dev-cam, Start = pause, A+B+X+Y+Start = quit, stick X = steer, stick Y = fwd/back on foot, D-pad = steer override).

Desktop needs no change — it is keyboard-only (W = throttle, S = brake) and has no left/right levers to swap.

Rebuilds clean, no warnings; 7/7 tests pass.

Note for the pending log harness: assert R drives *forward* and L drives *reverse/slow*, on both a standard pad (0/255) and a VMU (true analog).

comments.author: mcp-agent
comments.text: Closed: Dreamcast input mapping corrected — right trigger accelerates (R), left trigger brakes (L). Matches requested console convention and PSP mapping; preserved uncommitted changes (input_dc.c). Verification: cross-build clean, tests pass.

close_reason: Done: R accelerates (right lever), L brakes (left lever); role-based naming/edge tracking, mode-aware (vehicle-only levers, foot=stick only), KOS stick/trigger semantics handled, unplugged pad neutralises safely. Cross-builds clean, 7/7 tests pass.

title: PSP GU whole-triangle drops (ocean + terrain)

comments.author: mcp-agent
comments.text: Fixed in src/backend/psp/render_gu.c, mirroring render_dc.c. Root cause (verified numerically with .scratch/clip_probe.c, a copy of the exact clip path driven by a realistic chase camera): (1) clip_tri_near classified inside as z+w >= -PSP_CLIP_EPS and S-H crossings landed exactly on z+w=0, so after the (proj*view)^-1 round trip the GE saw vertices at z+w = -4.8e-7 (measured worst) - outside - and its no-clip rule dropped the WHOLE triangle: ocean tiles nearest the camera. Fix: shifted distances (dp = z+w - PSP_CLIP_EPS, inside iff dp >= 0, t = dp/(dp-dq)) so every emitted vertex is strictly inside by ~1e-4 (measured worst z+w = +9.87e-05, w = 0.10005 after round trip), same pattern as DC's dc = w - DC_CLIP_EPS. (2) present_mesh never clipped at all - any terrain/house mesh triangle straddling the eye or near plane went straight to the GE and was dropped whole. Fix: ClipVert gained u/v (lerped), emit_tri refactored to transform_tri returning the clipped polygon, present_mesh pre-checks every vertex and keeps the indexed submission when fully inside, otherwise expands triangles through the same clip path (textured + untextured variants), exactly like render_dc.c routes meshes through dc_emit_tri. Verification: .scratch/clip_probe.c passes (was failing with z+w < 0 before the fix); psp cross-build clean, zero warnings; EBOOT.PBP rebuilt; PPSSPPSDL ran 8s with no crash; desktop meson test 10/10. docs/render-psp.md near-clip bullet updated. Visual confirmation (no more vanishing tiles/terrain) is on the user in PPSSPP.

comments.author: mcp-agent
comments.text: Six-plane rework supersedes the earlier near-only fix. Root cause for remaining drops (PPSSPP + hardware, ocean + terrain; unaffected on desktop/DC): the GE's T&L has no clipper - with clip planes disabled it discards a WHOLE primitive when any vertex has W<=0, screen Z outside [0,65536), or screen X/Y outside the 0..4096 guard band (|x/w|<=8.533, |y/w|<=15.059), not just z+w<0 - which is why shrinking the 1e-4 epsilon changed nothing (float24 roundoff is ~0.01 absolute, so PSP_CLIP_EPS is now 0.1, ~10x that; big near-camera ocean tiles sprawled past the guard band and vanished whole). Fix in src/backend/psp/render_gu.c: clip_eval evaluates all six plane distances per object-space vertex (near z+w, far w-z, left/right x+/-GX*w, bot/top y+/-GY*w with GX=8 GY=14 inside the band); clip_obj_tri classifies (code = OR of source plane bits, code 0 = untouched fast path), S-H clip_pass only over violated planes with affine distances riding along, no (proj*view)^-1 round trip (keeps hardware fog); clip_code_tint colours clipped polys by their code (odd multipliers mod 256, floored bright, alpha 1) so you can see which planes fired - code 0 keeps normal colour; emission staged into sceGuGetMemory chunks (CLIP_STAGE=150, never stack - D-cache coherency), poly buffers CLIP_MAX_POLY=9; present_recorded + present_mesh classify against all six planes (screen path passes clip_mvp=NULL). Verification: .scratch/clip_probe.c rewritten for the six-plane path - all planes fire (near/left/right/bot/top in both chase cameras), worst z+w=0.65, w-z=0.20, w=0.42, guard-band margin=0.23, every emitted vertex inside all six, winding mismatches=0, tint matches clip_code_tint; psp cross-build clean; desktop meson test 10/10; PPSSPP ran 8s clean (full boot, clean shutdown); docs/render-psp.md near-clip bullet replaced with the six-plane table + guard-band explanation. Visual confirmation on hardware is on the user.

title: Low-poly hover car model
description:
Faceted low-poly hover car: wedge hull, canopy, fin, hover pods/skirts, hard textures with flat colour panels. Built in code or from an asset file, using vertex colours plus one or two textures.

KEEP IT VERY SIMPLE (art direction, user-confirmed): the car can be a handful of boxes/capsules — a stretched wedge box hull, a small dark box canopy, one fin, two side pods. NO wheels, NO rolling parts — it hovers, and the hover clearance (visible gap under the hull) is what sells that.

## Design
Static, hand-authored vertex data in src/car_mesh.c (fixed-function friendly — no VBOs):

- Hull: single box stretched/wedged (front low, rear high), 8-10 silhouette verts. Do NOT share verts across facets — duplicated verts per facet give hard edges and flat normals (the PS1 look).
- Canopy: small dark box (~0.10, 0.12, 0.16), slightly inset.
- Fin + two side hover pods/skirt plates (plain boxes, grey/white panels).

title: Revisit frame caps when island content lands (16k verts / 512 draws)
description:
Context: R_MAX_VERTS 16384 / R_MAX_DRAWS 512 (src/core/render.h:24). Ocean alone is 6400 verts unculled (40x40 quads); the F3 overlay shows current usage. Terrain grid + props + buildings + NPCs (island1-39q6, island1-urkr, ...) will push against the caps.

Options when needed: grow caps (RVertex is 9 floats = 36 bytes; 16k verts = 576 KB per frame buffer), chunk+stream terrain like the ocean, cull harder via the frustum module (see frustum issue), or shrink the vertex format (see the lit/normals decision).
Also note r_text_2d() emits one quad per pixel-run - long HUD strings grow verts; fine today.
Done when: after island content lands, the F3 overlay shows headroom on the worst-case camera angle; caps raised or content streamed accordingly.

comments.author: mcp-agent
comments.text:
## Numbers (2026-10-03)

- RVertex = 9 floats = 36 bytes; R_MAX_VERTS 16384 → 576 KB per frame buffer; R_MAX_DRAWS 512.
- Ocean 40x40 = 1600 cells = 6400 verts unculled; the F3 overlay shows OCEAN drawn/total cells (frustum culling typically keeps ~1/3-1/2).
- Other growth pressure: terrain grid (island1-39q6), props/buildings, characters (island1-urkr), the wake ribbon (64 trail points → 252 verts), billboards, and r_text_2d() which emits one quad per pixel-run (a 48-char string at scale 2 is hundreds of quads).

## Options when needed

- Raise caps: 1 MB+ is fine on desktop; on PSP the frame lives in main RAM (32 MB), not VRAM, so it is cheap there too; on DC likewise (system RAM).
- Chunk + stream terrain like the ocean: cull whole chunks with the frustum module (island1-mc2v) before recording.
- Shrink the vertex format: the lighting decision (island1-agob, remove lit / no normals) is step one; pack colours to u8x4 and UVs to u16 → 36 → 20 bytes; the PSP/DC backends repack natively anyway.
- Split the frame into multiple passes if draws dominate.

## Console note

PSP/DC handle 512 draws fine if batched (TA lists / display lists) — the caps mostly protect the desktop recorder and its flat arrays. Keep both generous.

Not urgent: the F3 overlay shows current usage; revisit after island content lands.

Change:
- Frame-level scissor in RenderFrame (int scissor_enabled; int scissor[4]; in px) - one scissor per pass is enough; per-draw scissor can come later.

- DC backend (island1-fo7c): user clip in the polygon header (PVR_USERCLIP_INSIDE/OUTSIDE, KOS dc/pvr/pvr_header.h) - a native scissor-like clip area; modifier volumes (pvr_modifier_commit_zclip) for per-pixel volume clipping if ever needed.

comments.author: mcp-agent
comments.text:
## Audit context (2026-10-03, docs/render.md)

No glScissor anywhere; the desktop state manager diffs lighting/fog/texture/blend/depth/cull but has no scissor field. Needed when HUD content (island1-n7to) adds a minimap viewport, splitscreen or clipped panels; also handy for the dev overlay region.

## Hardware mapping (verified against SDK sources)

- Desktop: glScissor + set_enabled(GL_SCISSOR_TEST, ...) in gfx_set() — the pattern exists.
- PSP: native — sceGuScissor(x,y,w,h) + sceGuEnable(GU_SCISSOR_TEST) (GU_SCISSOR_TEST = 2; pspsdk asserts the region within 480x272; the scissor sample demonstrates per-region drawing).
- Dreamcast: BETTER than first assumed — the polygon header has a user clip mode, PVR_USERCLIP_DISABLE / INSIDE / OUTSIDE (KOS dc/pvr/pvr_header.h). PVR_USERCLIP_INSIDE keeps only pixels inside a clip area — a native scissor-like per-polygon clip, no modifier volumes needed for this. Modifier volumes (pvr_modifier_commit_zclip) remain the option for per-pixel volume clipping.

## Design notes

- Frame-level scissor in RenderFrame (int scissor_enabled; int scissor[4] px, GL-style bottom-left origin) — one active scissor per frame is enough for a minimap; per-draw scissor can come later if splitscreen lands.
- Scissor interacts with clear: clear the full screen before enabling, or honour the scissor in the clear too (document which).
- On DC the backend stamps clip_mode + clip area into each header while the scissor is active.

Done when: a minimap rect renders clipped to its region on desktop; other passes unaffected (no state bleed); mapping survives the backend split.

title: Analog input: throttle/brake axes, stick steer, on-foot analog
description:
Move the driving and walking inputs onto analog axes so the console backends can use triggers + sticks as the primary controls (user direction).

Context: today ACT_THROTTLE/ACT_BRAKE are digital actions and only steering is an axis (AX_STEER). On Dreamcast/PSP the analog stick is the main input and the L/R triggers are analog, so throttle/brake must be axes too, and on foot the stick should drive movement.

Changes:
- input.h: add AX_THROTTLE (0..1 accelerate / forward) and AX_BRAKE (0..1 brake/reverse). Keep ACT_THROTTLE/ACT_BRAKE digital for menus/dev and as a keyboard fallback.
- input.c: axes are absolute levels, already handled; just extend the enum. Counts update automatically.
- desktop input_glfw.c: drive W/UP -> AX_THROTTLE, S/DOWN -> AX_BRAKE (digital action still fired), A/D/arrows -> AX_STEER as today. Document that console triggers map here.
- game.c drive_car(): throttle = maxf(AX_THROTTLE, held(ACT_THROTTLE)); brake likewise; keep AX_STEER. walk_player(): forward = throttle - brake (analog), turn = AX_STEER (analog), so a stick walks smoothly.
- input test: assert AX_THROTTLE/AX_BRAKE behave as absolute levels.

Note for psp/dc input backends: stick X -> AX_STEER, L/R analog -> AX_THROTTLE/AX_BRAKE; on foot the same stick/triggers drive movement.

Done when: analog throttle/brake reach the car and walking with no digital key involved (verified in test), desktop W/S still work, all tests pass.

title: Remove dead lighting plumbing (or add normals + vertex lighting)
description:
Context: audit (docs/render.md) found the `lit` flag can never be true: RVertex has no normals (src/core/render.h:27), r_mesh() forces lit=0 (src/core/render.c:117), all immediate-path draws set lit=0, and draw_state_from() maps out->lighting = d->lit while the mesh path overrides gs.lighting = 0 (src/backend/desktop/render_gl.c:111). setup_lights() (src/backend/desktop/gfx_gl.c:93) configures GL_LIGHT0/1, COLOR_MATERIAL, SEPARATE_SPECULAR_COLOR, NORMALIZE - all dead state.

Options:
A (recommended): delete the plumbing - drop RDraw.lit, GfxState.lighting, setup_lights(), and the unused `lit` params in mesh.h (mesh_quad/mesh_add_quad signatures). Art direction (docs/art-direction.md) wants colour from texture + vertex colour, not light.
B: add normals to RVertex (+3 floats, or packed s8x3 - vertex size matters on PSP/DC) and wire fixed-function Gouraud for authentic PS1 per-vertex lighting. More authentic but bigger vertices and a lighting pass to tune.

Decision must land before console vertex formats are frozen (island1-fo7c, island1-gi02 pack RVertex natively).
Done when: either the flag/lights are gone and the build is clean, or meshes carry normals and a lit draw renders Gouraud-shaded on desktop.

comments.author: hayden
comments.text: Lighting decision (2026-10-03): "we probably aren't going to use opengl lighting, or if we do it will be per vertex without smooth. this game is likely going to take place in the sun and we are targetting older retro hardware so the lighting model can be simpler."

comments.author: mcp-agent
comments.text:
## Interpretation and consequences (of the decision above)

- No GL fixed-function lighting pipeline (setup_lights, GL_LIGHT0/1, COLOR_MATERIAL, Gouraud interpolation). If runtime lighting is ever added it stays CPU-side at vertex/face granularity, baked into colours before recording — never per-pixel, never GL-smooth-interpolated.
- Sun-lit scene: one warm key direction baked into face shades at mesh build time (mesh_add_box already shades top-brightest, bottom-darkest) + per-draw tint covers the whole look.
- Landing decision = option A from the description: DELETE the plumbing. Drop RDraw.lit, GfxState.lighting, setup_lights() (src/backend/desktop/gfx_gl.c:93-124) and the unused `lit` params in the mesh.h signatures (mesh_quad/mesh_add_quad, mesh.h:15,22).

## Proof the plumbing is dead today

- RVertex has no normals (src/core/render.h:27) — GL lighting cannot evaluate.
- r_mesh() forces lit=0 (src/core/render.c:117); every immediate-path draw sets lit=0.
- draw_state_from() maps out->lighting = d->lit but the mesh path overrides gs.lighting = 0 (src/backend/desktop/render_gl.c:111) — the lit path is unreachable for both draw kinds.
- setup_lights() configures GL_LIGHT0/1, GL_COLOR_MATERIAL, GL_SEPARATE_SPECULAR_COLOR, GL_NORMALIZE — nothing can ever enable lighting.

## Why before the console split

island1-fo7c (DC) and island1-gi02 (PSP) pack RVertex natively — removing `lit` (and NOT adding normals) freezes the vertex format at 9 floats (36 bytes), which both backends then repack (PSP: u8/s16 VTYPE attributes; DC: ARGBPACKED colours). Adding normals later would grow every backend's vertex format.

Done when: the flag/lights/params are gone, build is clean, zero behavioural change (lighting was never on), and docs/render.md (lighting section) matches the code.

title: Delivery loop state machine
description:
Sandbox loop with no timer: idle free-roam, pickup package, deliver to the marked resident, award a small score/floating text, then pick a new random recipient. Driving back to the depot is always allowed.

## Design
src/delivery.c/h, stepped on the 60Hz tick (island1-mmap):

    typedef enum { DL_IDLE, DL_CARRYING, DL_DELIVERING } DeliveryPhase;

    typedef struct {
        DeliveryPhase phase;
        int  target_house;     // index into buildings[]
        uint32_t delivered;    // running score
        float deliver_timer;   // DL_DELIVERING countdown
    } DeliveryState;

Transitions:

    DL_IDLE:      near depot (dist < 4 m) AND package available AND input_pressed(ACT_PICKUP)
                  -> spawn parcel on car, pick target house (seeded RNG, reject within 40 m of car), spawn beacon (island1-p3qz), phase = DL_CARRYING
    DL_CARRYING:  dist(car, doorway(target)) < 3.0 AND input_pressed(ACT_DELIVER)
                  -> phase = DL_DELIVERING, deliver_timer = 0.6
    DL_DELIVERING: timer -= dt; at 0 -> delivered++, floating "+1" via island1-5stj,
                  phase = DL_IDLE, parcel despawned; re-pickup at depot allowed immediately

No timer/timeout anywhere — sandbox. Random pick uses the same PRNG family as island1-39q6 for determinism.

Expose for the HUD (island1-n7to): phase, target house id, delivered count; HUD strings: "GO TO DEPOT" / "DELIVER TO HOUSE N" / "DELIVERING...".

## Done when
Full loop pickup -> drive -> deliver -> "+1" -> beacon moves to a new house works end-to-end; re-pickup after delivery is possible; state never dead-ends (IDLE with no package but depot reachable is always valid).

comments.author: mcp-agent

title: Auto-patch every ISO with retail SU14 field (iso_uxa.py wired into build_psp_iso.sh)

comments.author: mcp-agent
comments.text: HW A/B settled the root cause: the retail 14-byte XA system-use field (000000000d/8d555841000000000000) is what enables firmware open() of names longer than 8.3 — long+SU works perfectly, long+no-SU ENOENT, 8.3+no-SU also works. Research on native mkisofs: no option injects these bytes directly; -xa and -XA emit XA system use where DIRECTORY records match retail byte-for-byte (8d555841...) but FILE records differ (mkisofs 09115841 vs retail 0d555841), -U -xa works together but inherits the same file mismatch; no flag tunes those bytes. Since only the retail byte pattern is hardware-proven (island_long_uxa), kept iso_uxa.py and wired it into build_psp_iso.sh right after mkisofs so EVERY canonical image is patched automatically (= user requirement: all ISOs like island_long_uxa). Rewrote the stale "8.3 constraint" comment in build_psp_iso.sh with the new proven rules (patch mandatory; long names fine after patch; mkisofs -xa non-equivalence noted) and added the same rationale to iso_uxa.py docstring. Verified: patched 32 records/6 dirs, 20/20 non-dot entries carry retail SU14 including parcel.png, TITLE unchanged 'island', PPSSPP smoke clean (dname=parcel.png, no crash, textures ok). Note: build_psp_variants.sh base variant remains a deliberate no-SU diagnostic control; uxa variant patch now redundant with canonical but harmless.

title: On-foot walking animation: leg/arm swing
description:
Drive the leg/arm swing in code from walk speed — PS1-style in-place animation, no skeletal data.

## Design
- Swing = sin(phase) * AMPLITUDE with phase += speed * FREQ * dt (step frequency scales with speed)
- Arms counter-phase legs; amplitude and frequency both go to 0 when idle
- Walk cycle: legs ±35°, arms ∓30°; head bob y = |sin(phase)| * 0.05
- Walking controller (island1-7duk) fills the pose each tick; humanoid_draw applies via glRotatef at pivots
- Later: talking pose (arms crossed) and delivery reaction (one arm raised waving) as named pose targets — lerp swing angles between poses

Geometry stays basic per art direction: box limbs, box head — the swing sells the motion, not the mesh.

## Done when
Standing still -> fully static; walking -> steps in time with speed (no foot slide, <10%); no pop at speed 0; pose targets blend without visible snaps.

title: Dreamcast render backend (PERFUM + TILE2)
description:
Dreamcast render backend: implement RenderAPI (island1-1dtz) with the native KOS PVR Tile Accelerator (pvr_* API). Decided (user, 2026-10-03): NO GLdc - native PVR TA only. (The earlier PERFUM/TILE2 names do not exist in KOS; the real surface is pvr_poly_*/pvr_prim, with native pvr_sprite_* as a later bonus.)

- Full contract: docs/render-dc.md (hardware facts verified against KallistiOS)
- Opaque/TR/punch-through polygon lists chosen from the draw flags; TA sorts within lists (no painter's sorting from us)
- CPU transforms (KOS matrices are transposed vs GL); screen-space TA vertices, y down; W-buffer z = znear/w in (0,1] with PVR_DEPTHCMP_GREATER
- Near-plane clip (Sutherland-Hodgman vs w>eps) - the TA produces garbage for vertices behind the eye
- Fog: GL linear formula baked into vertex colours (PVR fog table units unverified - revisit on emulator)
- 16-bit textures (RGB565 / ARGB1555 for masked cutouts), twiddled, PVR_FILTER_NEAREST
- Backend v1 written: src/backend/dreamcast/{render_dc,texture_dc,input_dc,main_dc}.{c,h} + meson platform option + sh4-dreamcast-kos cross file
Done when: the desktop game's frame renders 1:1 in redream/NullDC or on hardware; verify culling winding, W-buffer z and fog look.

comments.author: mcp-agent
comments.text:
Flycast bring-up log (2026-10-03), after the first real boot:

- Freeze on boot: pvr_init_defaults() enables only OP+TR bins (PT = PVR_BINSIZE_0 = disabled) and pvr_list_begin(PVR_LIST_PT_POLY) on a disabled list stalls the PVR. Fixed: pvr_init() with opb_sizes {16, 0, 16, 0, 16} (OP+TR+PT), vertex_buf 512KB, autosort on. Also removed the explicit pvr_wait_ready() before the scene — the KOS examples loop straight into pvr_scene_begin() (it waits internally; pvr_wait_ready before any frame has rendered can stall).
- Winding: empirically the TA's winding sense matches the GL winding AS SEEN (no y-flip inversion) — R_CULL_BACK must map to PVR_CULLING_CW, not CCW. Verified in Flycast by the user.
- Ocean missing: two causes fixed. (1) The ocean quads' geometric normal pointed DOWN (emit order gave cross = (0,-1,0)), so the camera above saw the GL back face and cull NONE rendered two exactly-coincident faces at identical depth — the PVR's opaque compare mislikes that (desktop LEQUAL overdraw is harmless). Fixed in game.c: emit order flipped to normal-up + R_CULL_BACK (single-sided; consistent on both platforms under the empirical winding rule). (2) Screen-space draws used z=0 — infinity in the ISP's perspective/W-buffer math. Fixed: per-draw screen-space z — HUD = 1.0 (closest, sorts on top within TR), sky = znear/fog_end (farthest non-zero).
- Build: meson cross build works (build-dc + sh4-dreamcast-kos, cglm subproject cross-compiles with kos-cc gcc 15.2.0; needs c_std=gnu17 — KOS headers use C11 alignas). mkdcdisc is now a meson custom target ('island-cdi', mirrors the PSP EBOOT pattern): island.elf -> scrambled 1ST_READ.BIN + IP.BIN + assets/ -> island.cdi. -d (not -D) keeps the assets/ dir name on the disc matching the loader's fallback.
- Pipeline: meson compile -C build-dc produces build-dc/src/island.elf + island.cdi; Flycast boots it (KOS v2.3.0, 640x480 VGA, iso9660 mount OK).
- Note: the older KOS in this toolchain names the scene calls pvr_scene_finish()/pvr_wait_ready(), NOT pvr_scene_end()/pvr_wait_sync() (the latter are from newer KOS/docs).
- Still open: verify the full frame 1:1 (fog look, wake, HUD) in Flycast; native sprites (pvr_sprite_*) as a later bonus.

title: firmware file-access probe matrix in boot report

comments.author: mcp-agent
comments.text: Disassembly of newlib glue in our own ELF settled the design: getcwd = pure memcpy from static global (0x1e6430, never queries kernel); chdir = __path_absolute -> sceIoDopen (validates dir) -> sceIoChdir (kernel sync) -> strcpy into static cache; _open = __path_absolute -> sceIoOpen. So fopen already IS sceIoOpen underneath (abs-expanded); raw sceIoOpen with relative paths is worse (NOCWD 0x8002032c). Hardware reported chdir ok + rel probe missing => abs-open outcome unknown, so boot_report now probes 5 ways: rel stdio+errno, abs USRDIR stdio+errno, ctl SYSDIR/EBOOT.BIN stdio+errno (disc0 user-open discriminator), abs raw sceIoOpen code, sceIoDopen+dread listing first 4 dnames (firmware-visible names/case). buf bumped 1024->2048. BUG FIXED en route: probe block's local 'int n = 0' (dname counter) shadowed the ADD accumulator n -> snprintf(buf+0) clobbered report from offset 0 and its NUL truncated file to 31 bytes; renamed to 'shown'. PPSSPP ISO smoke: full report restored, all probes ok, dname=grass_64/hull_32/metal_32/parcel_32.png, ISO repacked 1081344 bytes.

title: PSP render backend (GUM + GE)
description:
PSP render backend: implement RenderAPI (island1-1dtz) with GUM (camera/matrices) + GE (vertex submission).

- GUM for view/projection + model matrices; GE DRAW primitives for meshes
- No fixed-function lighting on PSP: rely on baked vertex colours from core meshes (island1-1dtz constraint)
- No hardware fog in GUM/GE -> CPU vertex-colour fog: blend per-vertex colour toward fog colour by distance, using the same FrameFog values as desktop so the look matches
- One texture per mesh, affine mapping, NEAREST; billboards + 2D via GE quads / 2D blits

comments.author: mcp-agent
comments.text:
Render backend contract written: docs/render-psp.md (2026-10-03) — verified against pspdev/pspsdk (src/gu). Key facts for implementation:

- Primitives: GU_POINTS/LINES/LINE_STRIP/TRIANGLES/TRIANGLE_STRIP/TRIANGLE_FAN/SPRITES — there is NO quad primitive (sceGuDrawArray asserts prim <= GU_SPRITES). R_QUADS expands to 2 tris each CPU-side.
- GU_SPRITES = native 2-vertex "filled blocks" — perfect for r_rect_2d/HUD; works with GU_TRANSFORM_3D too (the sprite sample draws 3D billboards with it).
- Native alpha test (GU_ALPHA_TEST + sceGuAlphaFunc(GU_GREATER, ref*255, 0xff)) and native scissor (sceGuScissor + GU_SCISSOR_TEST) — cover two of the audit gaps.
- GE fog is LINEAR ONLY: sceGuFog(near, far, color), no mode/density — the standing "No hardware fog in GUM/GE → CPU vertex-colour fog" decision in this issue's description can be dropped; sceGuFog with the frame's start/end + sky colour matches desktop exactly. (Corrects the description above.)
- Native 4x4 dither (GU_DITHER + sceGuSetDither; sceGuStart installs a default) — the PS1 dithered look is free.
- Winding: pspsdk samples use GU_CW (their meshes are CW); our meshes are GL_CCW — set GU_CCW explicitly and verify culling in the emulator.
- Vertex formats: flexible VTYPE packing (f32/s16/u16/s8/u8 per attribute) — repack RVertex natively.
- Max texture 512x512, swizzled, one stage; 2 MB VRAM shared by framebuffers + depth + lists + textures.
- CPU frustum culling is mandatory (island1-mc2v) — the GE vertex-processes submitted polys even when clipped.
- API-level gaps that feed this backend: alpha test (island1-qb9x), scissor (island1-4t0s), tex_env (island1-01nc), fog mode (island1-pqhi).

comments.text:
PSP render backend implemented (src/backend/psp/), built and packaged; boots in PPSSPP.

Files:
- render_gu.{h,c}: sceGu flusher. Projection/view fed straight from r_frame() via sceGuSetMatrix(GU_PROJECTION/GU_VIEW); cglm mat4 == ScePspFMatrix4 layout. Per-mesh GU_MODEL = d->world. R_QUADS/LINES expanded into scratch packed-vertex buffers (GU_TEXTURE_32BITF|GU_COLOR_8888|GU_VERTEX_32BITF, meshes add GU_INDEX_16BIT). Screen-space uses a [0,1] ortho via sceGumOrtho + depth test off (GL bottom-left origin).

- main.c + psp_setup.h: module boilerplate, fixed 60 Hz loop.

Conventions chosen: GU_PSM_5650 double-buffered framebuffer (512 stride) for the native dither look; GU_PSM_4444 depth; reversed depth (sceGuDepthRange(65535,0), clear 0, GU_GEQUAL); GU_CCW front face; HW fog via sceGuFog(near,far,sky) -- so the description's "CPU vertex-colour fog" note is obsolete; baked vertex colours, GU_LIGHTING never enabled.

comments.text: Post-close update (real hardware): rendering was garbled on a real PSP even though PPSSPP was correct. title: Ocean: distance-graded camera-centred grid (cut ocean verts)
description:
Follow-up to island1-jfde. Even after frustum culling the ocean still emits a uniform ~10m grid (OCEAN_N 40 x OCEAN_SIZE 400 = 1600 cells / 6400 verts base, ~349 cells / 1396 verts after cull in the smoke view). Improve:

- Camera-centred grid (recentre on the view eye x/z each frame) so the detailed area always surrounds the player and the plane can shrink to just past the fog horizon (FOG_END 220) instead of a fixed 400m box centred at origin (which shows an edge if the car drives past +/-200).
- Distance-graded axis mapping so cell size grows with distance: one regular NxN topology (shared vertices, NO T-junction cracks) mapped through offset(u) = R*(SKEW*u + (1-SKEW)*u^3), u in [-1,1]. Fine (~12m) near the eye, coarse (~40m) at the fogged rim.
- Make the flat-shade colour hash world-based (hash cell centre world coords) instead of grid indices, so colours stay put while the tessellation slides with the camera.
- Keep frustum cull; optionally skip cells fully beyond FOG_END.

Planned constants: OCEAN_N 25 (24x24 = 576 cells base), OCEAN_R 260, OCEAN_SKEW 0.55. Expected ~2x fewer ocean verts in view while extending coverage to the fog horizon. Waves + faceted PS1 look preserved.

title: Ocean plane with scrolling water texture
description:
Large ocean plane at sea level: scrolling hard-edged water texture with NEAREST sampling, two-layer offset for motion, colour grading toward the horizon and matching fog colour so the plane edge is invisible. Buoyant hover behaviour here is what makes the car read as floating.

## Design
- 300x300 unit quad centered on origin, y = SEA_LEVEL (0.0). Drawn before terrain; depth test on, no blending.
- Texture: hard-edged 64x64 water tile from island1-802h, GL_RGBA, GL_NEAREST, no mipmaps (mip shimmer kills the era look).
- Motion: the GL 1.2/1.5 compat context has NO multi-texture, so the "two-layer offset" becomes one trick: scroll the single layer in world space and tie the rate to the car's velocity — classic PS1 water.

    // world-space scroll, applied to the 4 quad's texture coords
    vec2 s = { car.pos[0] * 0.02f + t * 0.06f, car.pos[2] * 0.02f };
    texcoord = worldcoord * 0.5f + s;      // mod 1.0 in the vertex

  Net effect: water crawls when idle, rushes backwards at speed — no UV animation needed in a shader.
- Color: deep blue-green base (~0.05, 0.32, 0.38) via vertex colors, brighter toward center; the horizon seam disappears because fog color == sky color and fog END lands before the plane edge (see island1-a440).
- Foam/spray from wake is separate (island1-5stj) and renders after this pass.

## Done when
Scrolling freezes when the car stops; no visible plane edge from any camera height or angle; no mip shimmer when the car bobs.

title: Architecture: strict core/backend layering + per-platform build targets
description:
Split the codebase so gameplay/input logic and rendering never mix: core is platform-agnostic C; each platform (desktop now; PSP + Dreamcast later) supplies a thin backend that links in. One codebase compiles to all targets.

## Layout
    src/core/                 # platform-agnostic: input.h (contract), car, delivery,
                              # walking, player, terrain, ocean, dialog, camera math,
                              # mesh data, FrameScene
                              # NO GL/GLFW/PSPLIB/DreamOS headers here
    src/backend/desktop/      # main.c (window + loop), input_glfw.c, render_gl.c
    src/backend/psp/          # main_psp.c, input_psp.c, render_psp.c  (P3, later)
    src/backend/dc/           # main_dc.c,  input_dc.c,  render_dc.c  (P3, later)

## Rules
1. core includes nothing from backend/ and no platform/GL headers
2. One-directional flow: backend polls input -> core ticks -> core produces FrameScene -> backend renders it. Backend never mutates game state; core never calls draw.
3. FrameScene is the only payload crossing the layer: plain data (camera, fog, ordered list of draw items - mesh + transform + tint, billboards, 2D text/rects)
4. main() lives in the backend; core exposes `void game_tick(float dt)` + `const FrameScene* game_frame()`
5. meson: island_core static lib + one executable per platform target (desktop now)
6. Enforcement: a layering check greps core for platform headers/symbols (GL*, GLFW, glad, PSP/KOS, DreamOS/pvr) and must return nothing.

## Done when
Repo matches the layout; the desktop game builds and runs via run.sh/meson; the island_core target builds standalone; the layering check passes.

title: Render pass system with fixed-function state management
description:
Render passes as FrameScene emitters: core emits ordered draw items (sky/ocean/terrain/props/vehicle/particles/beacon/HUD) into the frame; the backend (RenderAPI, see render-abstraction issue) flushes them in order. State (fog, blend, 2D mode) is a flag on the item, not ad-hoc glEnable/glDisable.

## Design
Passes live in core as emitters:

    emit_sky(&frame), emit_ocean(&frame, t), emit_terrain(&frame),
    emit_props(&frame), emit_buildings(&frame), emit_vehicle(&frame, car),
    emit_particles(&frame), emit_beacon(&frame), emit_hud(&frame)

Each appends items with flags (fog on/off, alpha, 2D). The desktop backend diffs its own GL state between items — that's where today's gfx.c state manager goes (backend/desktop, NOT core). 2D/alpha items are self-contained (begin+end their own state), replacing push/pop semantics.

- Removes the ad-hoc glEnable(GL_LIGHTING)/glDisable pairs in render_ground/render_axes (src/render.c:89,125,131,133) into the backend flusher.
- Fog color == sky color so the horizon seam is invisible (island1-a440).

## Done when
No GL state management in core; toggling any single pass out leaves the rest rendering identically (no state bleed); desktop output pixel-identical to pre-refactor.

comments.author: mcp-agent
comments.text:
## Audit context (2026-10-03, docs/render.md)

Gribb-Hartmann plane extraction + conservative AABB test exist but are locked in src/core/game.c:272-324 (frustum_plane, extract_frustum, aabb_in_frustum) and used only by ocean cells (game.c:371). Car, parcel, wake and billboards are recorded unconditionally; island content (terrain island1-39q6, props, characters island1-urkr) would not be culled at all.

## Why it matters per platform

- Desktop: fine today (tiny scene, F3 shows usage), needed before island content pushes against R_MAX_DRAWS/R_MAX_VERTS (island1-41ct).
- PSP/DC: vertex throughput is THE bottleneck. HW clipping exists (GE clips polys; PVR TA clips) but the hardware still vertex-processes every submitted poly — culling before recording is the only culling that saves transform + submission work.

## Design details

- Keep the conservative AABB test (reject only when fully outside one plane) — matches the fog-heavy PS1 look, no pop-in at plane edges.
- Mesh gains world-space bounds: float center[3]; float radius; grown incrementally in mesh_make/mesh_add_quad. Cull with the transform applied: transform the center, scale the radius by the max scale factor of the world matrix (current meshes don't scale, but billboards/props might later).
- Sphere test (center+radius vs plane) is cheaper per draw than AABB; AABB stays for ocean cells.
- Extend the F3 overlay with a CULLED counter next to the OCEAN drawn/total cells counter.

Done when: frustum code lives in core with no duplicates, meshes carry bounds, car/parcel/props cull correctly (F3 counters), ocean behaviour unchanged.

comments.author: mcp-agent
comments.text: Done in src/backend/psp/render_gu.c: no GU_TRIANGLE_FAN anywhere. Recorded quads go out as one degenerate-joined GU_TRIANGLE_STRIP with per-quad strip order (q1,q2,q0,q3), which under GL strip parity (even i,i+1,i+2 / odd i+1,i,i+2) reproduces the source tris (q0,q1,q2) and (q0,q2,q3) exactly - winding matches the triangle-list path for any projected quad (an earlier (q0,q1,q3,q2) order used the wrong diagonal and flipped non-planar quads; stitched through Y = previous quad's last strip vert v[q-1] with b0 = Q[1], segment starts land on even indices). When any vertex crosses a clip plane the recorded draw degrades from the strip to a plain GU_TRIANGLES list through the six-plane S-H clip path (island1-1s8d); R_LINES is never submitted by game code. Verification: .scratch/clip_probe.c - real_tris == 2*segs on both chase cameras, winding mismatches = 0 (diagonal flips = 54 counted separately as a source-quad property, not a strip failure); psp cross-build clean; desktop meson test 10/10; PPSSPP ran 8s clean; docs/render-psp.md documents the strip order + parity rule.

comments.author: mcp-agent
comments.text:
## Verification correction (2026-10-03)

The original note "the console targets cannot express the other modes" was wrong for the Dreamcast. Verified against KOS:

- DC: fog is per-polygon-header (PVR_FOG_TABLE / PVR_FOG_VERTEX / PVR_FOG_TABLE2 / PVR_FOG_DISABLE, dc/pvr/pvr_header.h) and KOS exports pvr_fog_table_linear / _exp / _exp2 / _custom, pvr_fog_table_color, pvr_fog_far_depth and the PVR_FOG_DENSITY register. DC can do linear (table), exp and exp2 — and table fog is perspectively correct (built from an inverse-w depth table, pvr_fog_tables.h).
- PSP: GE fog is linear only — sceGuFog(near, far, color) has no mode/density parameter (verified: pspsdk src/gu/sceGuFog.c); GU_FOG is just an enable bit.
- Desktop: GL_LINEAR hardcoded at init (gfx_gl.c:36); GL 1.5 also has EXP/EXP2/density. The comment there (EXP default swallows everything) is good context for why the mode must match what the passes configure.

## Revised recommendation

Keep linear as the frame's only mode — it matches the PSP exactly and the art direction (docs/art-direction.md: linear fog, colour = sky_horizon). The DC could honour a hypothetical EXP mode (pvr_fog_table_exp) but we would never use it. Document linear-only (done in docs/render.md) rather than adding mode+density.

Done when: the linear-only contract is recorded (docs/render.md) and any non-linear attempt is rejected consistently or documented as desktop-only.

title: RenderAPI: per-draw alpha test for cutout textures
description:
Context: GL 1.5 audit (2026-10-03, docs/render.md) found only a `blend` flag in RDraw/GfxState. Cutout textures (tree canopies, fences, stippled spray per docs/art-direction.md) need per-pixel discard: cheaper than blending on every target and needs no transparent sorting.

Change:
- RDraw gains `int alpha_test;` + `float alpha_ref;` (default 0 = off; 0.5 typical). Mutually exclusive with `blend` per draw.
- Desktop (base island1-1dtz): GfxState gains the fields; gfx_set() does glEnable(GL_ALPHA_TEST)/glAlphaFunc(GL_GREATER, ref); render_gl draw_state_from() maps them.
- PSP backend (island1-gi02): native - sceGuEnable(GU_ALPHA_TEST) + sceGuAlphaFunc(GU_GREATER, ref, 0xff) (pspsdk pspgu.h: GU_ALPHA_TEST = 0).
- Dreamcast backend (island1-fo7c): native equivalent is the punch-through polygon list (PVR_LIST_PT_POLY) - submit alpha-tested draws there (KOS kernel/arch/dreamcast/include/dc/pvr/pvr_header.h).

Done when: a masked texture (e.g. tree canopy with holes) renders cut out on desktop with no sorting artefacts; the flag survives the backend split.

comments.author: mcp-agent
comments.text:
## Audit context (2026-10-03, docs/render.md)

The GL 1.5 fixed-function audit found no path to glAlphaTest: RDraw/GfxState carry only a `blend` flag, and draw_state_from() (src/backend/desktop/render_gl.c:77) pins every draw to blend/depth/cull. Meanwhile cutout textures are core to the art direction (docs/art-direction.md): tree canopies with holes, fences, stippled spray edges (island1-5stj). Alpha test is the right primitive for all of these — cheaper than blending on every target (no blend fill-rate, no transparent sorting) and it composes with the PS1 look (hard-edged cutouts).

## Hardware mapping (verified against SDK sources)

- PSP: GU_ALPHA_TEST = 0 state + sceGuAlphaFunc(int func, int value, int mask), GU_NEVER..GU_GEQUAL (pspsdk src/gu/sceGuAlphaFunc.c; the sprite sample uses sceGuAlphaFunc(GU_GREATER, 0, 0xff)). Reference is 0..255 with an AND mask — the backend converts from our 0..1 float.
- Dreamcast: punch-through polygon list PVR_LIST_PT_POLY (KOS dc/pvr/pvr_header.h) — native per-pixel alpha discard, no blending, and it sorts with the opaque pass, so no transparent-sorting artefacts.
- Desktop: glEnable(GL_ALPHA_TEST) + glAlphaFunc(GL_GREATER, ref) — add fields to GfxState and the diff in gfx_set().

## Design notes

- RDraw gains `int alpha_test;` + `float alpha_ref;` (default 0 = off, 0.5 typical). Keep alpha_test and blend mutually exclusive per draw — on DC they are literally different lists, so a draw cannot be both; assert it on desktop and document it.
- On DC the backend picks PT_POLY when alpha_test is set, TR_POLY when blend is set, OP_POLY otherwise — the list choice falls out of the flags.
- Related: island1-01nc (tex_env ADD for glow is a separate concern); island1-fo7c / island1-gi02 consume this flag.

Done when: a masked canopy texture renders cut out on desktop with no sorting artefacts when overlapping; the flag survives the backend split (test on PPSSPP/redream emulators).

## Correction: R accelerates, L brakes (user direction, 2026-10-05)

Supersedes the trigger direction in the comment above. The user asked for the usual console convention (Xbox/PlayStation put the accelerator on the **right** trigger), so the triggers are swapped:

  R (PSP_CTRL_RTRIGGER) -> AX_THROTTLE + digital ACT_THROTTLE   (vehicle only)
  L (PSP_CTRL_LTRIGGER)  -> AX_BRAKE + digital ACT_BRAKE         (vehicle only)

Both the axis (`input_psp.c:157-158`) and the digital twin (`update_triggers()`, input_psp.c:69-70) were swapped together, so the axes and the action fallback can never disagree. The edge trackers were renamed `s_prev_ltrig`/`s_prev_rtrig` -> `s_prev_throttle`/`s_prev_brake` so a future edit is keyed by role instead of by side — that is what made the swap easy to get right in the first place.

Everything else in the table is unchanged (Cross = boost, Square = interact, Triangle = vehicle, Start = pause, Home = quit, Select = dev-debug, Vol+/Vol- = dev-cam/dev-reset, nub X = steer, nub Y = fwd/back on foot, D-pad = steer override).

Desktop needs no change — it is keyboard-only (W = throttle, S = brake) and has no left/right triggers to swap. Rebuilds clean, no warnings; 7/7 tests still pass.

title: Display targets and aspect handling: 16:9 desktop/PSP, 4:3 Dreamcast
description:
Target display modes (user direction):
- Desktop: 16:9 (default window 1280x720; support 720p/1080p and other 16:9).
- PSP: 480x272 (16:9, 1.765:1).
- Dreamcast: 640x480 (4:3).

Camera/rendering requirement: keep the *horizontal* field of view consistent across aspects so a 4:3 Dreamcast does not crop content that is visible at 16:9 (important for objective beacons/HUD). Strategy chosen: treat the chase camera's FOV as referenced to 16:9; derive the effective vertical FOV per frame from the real aspect so the horizontal view matches 16:9 (desktop unchanged) and 4:3 shows more vertically rather than less horizontally. Implemented in chase_cam.c (vfov_for_aspect) and verified by an aspect-invariance test in tests/chase_cam_test.c.

Still to do:
- Decide whether the dev free-fly camera should use the same rule (currently vertical FOV, dev-only).
- HUD/safe-area audit at 4:3 (pixel offsets are top-left absolute; toast centres on view width and is fine; confirm nothing important sits outside the 4:3 safe area).
- PSP's 480x272 is 1.765:1, not exactly 16:9; verify no distortion at that exact aspect.
- Backends should report the true framebuffer size (desktop already does via glfwGetFramebufferSize).

title: PSP near-clip rewrite in render_gu.c

comments.author: mcp-agent
comments.text: Test of comment writing.

comments.author: mcp-agent
comments.text:
## What was broken in the WIP near clip (src/backend/psp/render_gu.c)

1. mat4_mul_vec4 read flat[0..3] (column 0 of a GL column-major matrix) as if it were row 0, so it multiplied by the transpose.
2. mat4_mul4 computed B*A^T instead of A*B (with B = I it returned A^T), so the value called "mvp" was actually proj*view^T.
3. The near-plane test was `z >= 0`. A GL perspective projection puts the eye plane at z + w = 0, so that test throws away the whole near half of the frustum (z/w in [-1,0)) - most of the scene disappears.
4. Emitted vertices were perspective-divided to NDC but submitted with GU_TRANSFORM_3D while apply_state installed the real proj/view, so the GE projected them a second time.
5. clip_vert_lerp assigned out->v twice and never interpolated colour.
6. The quad path could overrun its count*2 vertex reservation: a clipped triangle fans out to 6 vertices, so quads need 3*count.

comments.author: mcp-agent
comments.text:
## Fix

Keep the GE's real proj/view: hardware fog is derived from view space (PPSSPP emits `v_fogdepth = viewPos.z * coef`), so swapping in identity matrices for CPU-transformed draws would kill fog on the ocean and other recorded draws. Instead: transform each triangle to clip space, clip against `z + w >= 0`, then map the clipped vertices back through `(proj*view)^-1` to object space before writing them. `M^-1 (M obj) = obj` with w == 1, so the GE's forward transform lands exactly on the clipped clip-space vertex. Fully-inside triangles are emitted unchanged (no inverse), and screen-space draws skip the transform entirely (orthographic, w = 1, never crosses the plane).

`emit_tri` / `emit_v` / `clip_vert_from` absorb the quad-vs-triangle duplication, so `present_recorded` is 64 lines instead of 111, and the GE-state reset repeated in `render_init`/`render_present` is now `reset_ge_state()`.

Verified with a standalone harness in /tmp/clip_test.c covering: mat4_mul_vec4 vs. a hand-written GL column-major multiply, `mvp*inv == I`, near-plane sign for in-frustum / just-past-znear / between-eye-and-near / behind-eye points, object->clip->inverse->object round trip, 1-in/2-out -> 3 verts, 2-in/1-out -> 4 verts, fully-behind dropped, and NDC reproduction after the inverse+forward hop. PSP target builds clean (`meson compile -C build_psp`), desktop suite 8/8.

title: PSP renderer needs near-plane clipping for world-space draws
description:
The PSP GE's clipper behaves differently from the Dreamcast TA. Our DC backend does manual near-plane clipping for world-space triangles (dc_clip_near) before submitting; the PSP backend submits transformed vertices directly via sceGuDrawArray for meshes and builds GuVtx from recorded verts without explicit software near clipping. Vertices that go behind the near plane (w <= 0) can produce incorrect or disappearing geometry on hardware/PPSSPP in some cases.

## Acceptance
- Investigate PSP recorded path (render_gu.c present_recorded) and mesh path: do we need to clip against near plane before building display list vertices?
- Add conservative clipping where needed or document why not required.
- Test on PPSSPP and real hardware if available.
- Keep core platform-agnostic (clipping logic lives in backend/psp).

## Notes
Mentioned while debugging DC trail depth/visibility (island1-m4g4 follow-up).

title: Player mode state machine: on-foot/in-vehicle, entering and exiting
description:
Toggle between on-foot and in-vehicle. Car stays parked where you exit. Carried package transfers between modes.

## Design
src/player.c/h:

    typedef enum { MODE_ON_FOOT, MODE_IN_VEHICLE } PlayerMode;

    typedef struct {
        PlayerMode mode;
        vec3  pos; float heading;   // on-foot state
        float transition_t;         // 0.5 s crossfade
    } Player;
    // vehicle state lives in CarState (island1-9n0n)

Entering:
    near a car (dist < 3.0 m) AND |car.speed| < 1.0 m/s AND press ACT_BOARD
    -> hide humanoid, mode = IN_VEHICLE, camera blends to vehicle framing

Exiting:
    in vehicle AND |car.speed| < 1.0 m/s AND press ACT_EXIT
    -> place player beside car (car right vector * 1.2 m), mode = ON_FOOT,
       car stays put (vel = 0, no idle drift)

- Add ACT_BOARD/ACT_EXIT to input actions (island1-ibqg); both bound to F as one context key
- Carried package moves with the player; delivery target is not reset on mode switch (island1-draq)
- On-foot camera: reuse chase cam (island1-fnss) with distance 4.5 / height 1.9 (vs 7.0/3.2 in vehicle); lerp params during transition_t

## Done when
Enter/exit works anywhere (land or water) when stopped; no flicker between body and car during transition; on-foot camera framing matches PS1 references; carried package and target persist across the switch.
